newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania president urges battle against corruption.
newsitem.headline: Romania president urges battle against corruption.

text.p: Romanian President Emil Constantinescu vowed on Wednesday to wage an uncompromising battle against what he said was endemic corruption in order to secure international confidence in the country.
Making his first formal televised appeal since he defeated ex-communist Ion Iliescu in November elections, Constantinescu said corruption and crime "endanger national security".

He said authorities would sack corrupt officials and tighten laws against crime and urged lawyers, police, intelligence service agents and the army to use their powers fully to restore confidence in public institutions.
"If matters continue in the present direction, there is a danger of considerable economic and monetary havoc or of violence, armed attacks or Mafia-type settling of accounts," Constantinescu said.

"We will not launch a witch-hunt, but a war of defence. The enemy is already on our territory, draining resources, ignoring traditions and legitimate interests and whispering that any attempt to resist is futile, that theft in Romania is rampant and will remain so."

Constantinescu said foreign investors were deterred from coming to Romania by high-ranking officials extorting bribes. The equivalent of more than $100 million was siphoned out of the national economy each year by smugglers.
"Serious foreign investors had to pay in recent years huge sums of money to top state officials merely for the opportunity to open and develop businesses in Romania," he said.
"They often leave and invest in other countries. We are in this way deprived of funds for technology as well as jobs, credibility and respect on international markets."
He told viewers that he had asked prosecutors to inform him fully on the dimensions of crime and corruption and the reasons behind long legal delays in bringing culprits to justice.

Constantinescu had accused the government ousted in last November's election of widespread corruption. His new prime minister, Victor Ciorbea, has pledged to purge dishonest officials as he did during a brief term as mayor of Bucharest.
The government has set as its priorities the raising of living standards and integration into NATO and eventually the European Union.
Ministers are about to embark on negotiations to restore International Monetary Fund credits suspended last year.
The president issued his appeal after a meeting of the National Security Council which he heads created a "National Council of Action" to fight corruption and organised crime.
